title: Fast GHZ encoding with $1-o(1)$ fidelity
authors: Laura Shou, T. C. Mooney, Twesh Upadhyaya, Alexey V. Gorshkov
abstract: We prove that $(1-o(1))$-fidelity $N$-qubit Greenberger--Horne--Zeilinger (GHZ) encoding can be performed in time $O(\log N/N)$ using all-to-all 2-local Hamiltonians with bounded 2-qubit interaction terms. This saturates the theoretical lower bound $Ω(\log N/N)$, and by rescaling, also saturates the lower bound on signaling time for Hamiltonians with power-law interaction strengths $1/r^γ$, $γ<d$ in dimension $d$. The protocol uses spin-squeezing dynamics combined with quantum signal processing.
summary: This paper presents a theoretical protocol to generate highly entangled Greenberger–Horne–Zeilinger (GHZ) states on $N$ qubits with near-perfect fidelity. By ingeniously combining spin-squeezing dynamics with Quantum Signal Processing, the authors achieve a time complexity of $O(\log N/N)$, matching the best-known theoretical lower bound. This represents a significant advancement in the speed and reliability of quantum state preparation.
main_problem: The primary goal is to demonstrate a method for achieving Greenberger–Horne–Zeilinger (GHZ) encoding on $N$ qubits with high fidelity in a time complexity that saturates the theoretical lower bound.
main_result: The authors propose a protocol that achieves $(1-o(1))$-fidelity GHZ encoding in time $O(\log N/N)$, matching the established lower bound for all-to-all Hamiltonians.
method: The protocol combines spin-squeezing dynamics (Two-Axis Twisting, TAT) with Quantum Signal Processing (QSP) to efficiently implement the necessary unitary transformations.
model_or_system: The system is an $N$-qubit quantum processor governed by all-to-all 2-local Hamiltonians. The encoding maps a single-qubit state into the GHZ subspace via controlled unitary evolution.
key_observables: Fidelity of the GHZ state, time complexity $T$, and the separation of quantum state packets on the Bloch/Dicke sphere.
important_parameters: The system size $N$, the interaction strength decay exponent $\gamma$, and the time scales $O(\log N/N)$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the continuum limit approximation for the Gaussian packet core and assumes the QSP method accurately implements the required sign function.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the three steps of the protocol from previous work, while Figure 2 and Figure 3 detail the state evolution in the new, optimized protocol, showing packet separation on the Dicke sphere.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the theoretical lower bounds for GHZ encoding time, introduces the novel protocol combining TAT squeezing and QSP, and then rigorously analyzes the fidelity and time complexity through detailed mathematical derivations involving operator derivatives and error bounding.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, optimized quantum circuit implementation for generating highly entangled states (GHZ states) at the fastest possible rate, which is crucial for quantum communication and computation protocols.

The Husimi distribution of the current state of each packet is shown overlayed in log scale, using a Lambert azimuthal projection of the sphere with the center being the +Z pole. Note that due to the log scale, the packets in the third panel after the controlled X step are actually much more separated than they may appear. While not relevant for the protocol in [Yin25a], the red contours show the boundaries y = ±1/3, to compare with Figure 2.

Figure 2. Illustration of the TAT packet separation in the new protocol, which consists of the same steps as the start of the protocol from [Yin25a] shown in Figure 1, but with different squeezing and rotation parameters. The parameters used for the three steps are those in the table in Section 1.3 with a = 9/20, κ = 9, and M = 1000. The red contours show the boundaries y = ±1/3. In Step 1, we squeeze the state further than in Figure 1, while in Step 2, we do a shorter controlled X rotation.
